problem: "In a link element, href gives the destination and target=\"_blank\" opens it in a new tab." The chapter has already used link as the void element that attaches a stylesheet. That element has no target attribute and does not open anything in a new tab. The element that does this is the a (anchor) element. A student will carry the wrong model into the link/stylesheet discussion.
fix: "In an a element, href gives the destination and target=\"_blank\" opens it in a new tab. The head's link element also uses href, but there it names the file being attached, and it has no target attribute."

problem: "A comment ... never appears in the tree" and "Neither is an element and neither appears in the tree." Comments do appear in the DOM tree as comment nodes, and they are visible in the Elements panel the chapter tells students to open. The claim contradicts the chapter's own Inspect instruction.
fix: "A comment is not an element and shows nothing on the page, but it is still a node in the DOM tree and you will see it in the Elements panel. It is not counted when you count elements." Same correction in the trap: "Neither is an element, so neither is counted in the element tree."

problem: "Four things live there" is followed by five items: title, meta charset, meta viewport, link, and then the script element. The count does not match the list.
fix: Say "Several things live there" and keep the list, or state that the four are title, meta charset, meta viewport and link, and that script is one more that may sit in head.

where: Section 2, void elements; repeated in quiz Q2 answer
problem: "Their content arrives through attributes, so there is nothing to close." This is true of img, input, meta and link, but br and hr carry no data at all; their attributes only tune the element (for example the line break itself, or the rule's width).
fix: "They have no content and no end tag. In img, input, meta and link the data arrives through attributes; br and hr simply mark a break or a rule, and their attributes only tune it."

problem: "Written with the mark, two dashes, text, two dashes, mark" never says which mark, so the reader cannot actually type a comment from this description.
fix: Write the characters out: a comment starts with <!-- and ends with -->, for example <!-- notice board starts here -->.

problem:
Two small gaps. First, "Quotes may be dropped only when the value has no spaces" is incomplete: an unquoted value also may not contain \" ' = < > or a backtick, and may not be empty. Second, "closing a void element" is ambiguous: the self-closing slash in or
is valid HTML and not an error; only a separate end tag such as is wrong.
fix: Say: "Leave quotes on. An unquoted value cannot contain spaces, quotes, =, <, > or a backtick, and cannot be empty." And in the trap: "A trailing slash in is allowed; a separate end tag is the error."

problem: Two symptoms are stated wrongly. A page with no title shows the file name or the URL on the tab, not "Untitled". And a wrong declared character set produces garbled characters (Ã¢â€š¹ and the like), not empty boxes; boxes mean the font lacks the glyph.
fix: "The tab shows the file name or URL instead of 'Notices', and the rupee sign breaks into strange characters. Faults: title missing from head, and charset missing or wrong. Fix: add a non-empty title and put <meta charset=\"UTF-8\"> as the first child of head."
